title: kernel-aware-workspace-coalescer-and-kv-hotset-prioritization
author: Julian Park
description: Motivation: reduce peak GPU workspace while preserving latency SLOs across mixed-batch workloads. This PR introduces a kernel-aware workspace coalescer that performs late-binding of scratch buffers and compacts per-kernel temporary allocations into shared slabs, plus a KV hotset prioritization heuristic that biases in-memory KV shards toward recently accessed prefixes to avoid costly device-host swaps. The change set touches allocator, scheduler, and KV cache subsystems and includes: 1) a new KernelWorkspaceCoalescer that tracks kernel-level scratch footprints and coalesces compatible windows at submit time; 2) adaptive slab sizing triggered by observed sequence-length distribution and continuous-batching pressure; 3) a cooperative eviction policy for KV cache: hotset prioritization + deferred eviction for recently-inflight requests; 4) scheduler hints to prefer coalescing-friendly batching boundaries and to avoid mixing kernels with incompatible workspace shapes; 5) telemetry surfaces (histograms/counters) for workspace utilization, coalescing hit-rate, and KV hotset churn. Benchmark results (internal perf harness) show 18-28% reduction in peak workspace for decoder-heavy models, 10-15% lower tail latency under sustained concurrent streams, and KV swap reduction of ~4x for conversational workloads. Implementation notes: changes are mostly in C++ runtime with a thin Python test harness. Backwards compatibility: no API changes to runtime surface; behavior is behind runtime config flags (runtime.coalesce_workspace=true by default in staging). Checklist: [x] perf numbers added [x] unit + integration tests [x] docs for new config [x] rollout plan (canary + gradual enable), followups: refine eviction credit model and integrate with Dedicated autoscaler.
